**Reasoning (based on 500-iteration trends + reward-gradient structure):**

- **C4** leads already (task_score 7.19, max 7.45) and is still climbing fast (last-50 increment +0.42, the largest of any candidate). Crucially, it has the *strongest sustained gradient at high speed*: clipped-linear main term (3.0/12 m/s ≈ 0.25 per m/s) **plus** raw linear term (0.5 per m/s) **plus** an active sprint ramp above 5 m/s (≈0.14 per m/s) — roughly 3–4× the high-speed gradient of the others. The `upright × tanh(vx)` coupling keeps the ant from trading posture for speed, so it converts gradient into actual running rather than lunging.
- **C1** is a close second (6.54). Its speed gradient at ~7 m/s is only ≈0.23 per m/s (0.2 linear + a nearly saturated 6 m/s-temp tanh), and its task_score increments had already collapsed to +0.10 by iter 500, so it is flattening; it will likely saturate well below C4.
- **C2** (6.00) has a saturated tanh (1.5 weight, 6 m/s temp) plus a surge ramp that fully flattens at 9.5 m/s, so its high-speed gradient collapses to ~0.07 per m/s. Its heading/upright bonuses also mildly discourage leaning into a sprint. Better than C3 but limited.
- **C3** (5.83) trails despite an unbounded linear speed term: the upright (0.5) and height-preference terms reward a conservative, upright gait (body_forward decays to 0, up_z ≈ 0.84), and its score increments are the flattest (+0.22 in the last 50). Its speed shaping (1 m/s temp) is also nearly saturated, so the extra linear weight mostly buys reward scale rather than extra speed.

All four have comparable action/joint regularizer strength, so the differentiator is high-speed reward gradient and posture–speed coupling, both of which favor C4.
